answer: Each bonded identity is a vertex in the consensus graph, and signed equivocation across k coordinated identities creates up to k(k−1)/2 attributable pairs, so penalties scale as O(k²). Escrowed collateral and asymmetric depreciation make detection more costly than a linear fee: the coordinated swarm’s capital loss compounds exponentially, turning a seemingly broad knoll of disposable accounts into a canyon of shared risk.
